name: Murudeshwara Temple
deity: Shiva as Murudeshwara, on a headland above the Arabian Sea
period: A coastal Shiva shrine tied to the Atma Linga of Gokarna, renowned for its towering statue and gopura
dynasty: Ancient site, its great tower and statue built by modern patrons
summary: On a rocky headland thrusting into the Arabian Sea, Shiva is worshipped as Murudeshwara beneath a colossal seated statue and a soaring twenty-storey gopura — one of the coast's most striking sights.

sections.history: Murudeshwar stands on the Kanduka hill, a headland reaching into the Arabian Sea in Uttara Kannada. The shrine is bound to the legend of the Atma Linga of nearby Gokarna, and in modern times has been raised into one of the coast's grandest temple complexes.
sections.architecture: The temple is crowned by a Raja Gopura of some twenty storeys, among the tallest in India, and beside it rises a vast seated statue of Shiva overlooking the sea. The setting — sea on three sides, sky above — is the temple's signature.
sections.legends: By tradition the demon Ravana carried off the Atma Linga of Shiva, and was tricked by Ganesha into setting it down at Gokarna, where it fixed forever. The cloth that had covered the linga is said to have fallen at this place, which took the name Mrideshwara, or Murudeshwara.
sections.festivals: Maha Shivaratri is the great night here, drawing crowds to the sea-girt hill. Kartika and the temple's own car festival fill the year with worship beside the waves.
sections.experience: Few Indian temples sit so dramatically on the sea; pilgrims come for darshan of Murudeshwara and to stand beneath the great statue with the Arabian Sea spread on every side.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan and a midday break; Maha Shivaratri is busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Murudeshwar lies on the coast of Uttara Kannada in Karnataka, on the Konkan railway line and the coastal highway between Mangaluru and Karwar, with its own railway station.
